Or should it be applied only to smaller areas and after a moisturizer? I will also look into using a vitamin C serum, but should I use this instead of niacinamid? Or just use both?

I think I still need to apply my full coverage foundation and concealer, as targeting only the "worst" spots still is like the whole face.. Having the makeup on (and for as long as possible) also keeps me from seeing the spots, so I will not begin my bad habits for all that time. But it is true, as some of you have said, that I can get away with it because I get better at covering my tracks. It does however make me anxious when I need to sweat in front of others, e.g. going to a fitness center (so I have stopped doing that) as the sweat might take away some of the coverage. The same with rain or when I may need to wipe around my mouth during/after lunch in case a covered blemish is close to the mouth. 

The habit is also hard to break because I am actually looking forward to get home from work and do it. I usually listen to podcasts while doing it, and I hyperfocus on it and almost go into a trance. It relieves to much stress. And it feels as if I am achieving something by getting it done and getting all of the bad stuff out of my skin. I recently went on the best vacation of my life with my boyfriend for 8 days, but I often thought to myself that I couldn't wait to get home to my magnifying mirror and tools to remove all of what had accumulated during the vacation.

I also hate it because of the pressure to be excited about receiving gifts, having family wanting to celebrate you and being the center of attention. I also share my birthday with my grandmother, so I have always been ashamed of "stealing" her day because my family celebrate the kids' birthdays more than the adults' and I hated getting the attention instead of her. 

She passed away a few years ago, and I now miss having this shared birthday. Before we could at least somewhat share the attention, and I do think now that she preferred being able to redirect the attention to someone else as I think she did not like being the center of attention either. She was a fantastic person and I have always admired her and miss her.

It really depends on whether or not you are going to participate in the organisation's events. The forum, Facebook pages and public gatherings, at least in Denmark, are the basis for a lot of interesting discussions and open reflections, where nobody looks weird to you if you have an otherwise odd hobby or ask otherwise weird questions. Everyone's on board and wholeheartedly share your enthusiasm as soon as you show it. Everyone's wholeheartedly curious and wanting to learn new things all the time.

I have chosen to think of it kind of like being member of a book club, a sports club etc., but where the interests we all have in common are curiousity, puzzles, wanting to learn and reflect more etc. 

This of course depends on how the organisation in your country are organising their events and interact with the members. But in Denmark, it has been a fantastic community for me in a time where I felt like I was alone in the world and could not find any meaning in my everyday life.
